title: Scheme-theoretic image of a proper scheme in a separated one is proper
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $f:X\to S$ a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], $g:Y\to S$ a morphism which is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism] and locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $h:X\to Y$ a morphism with $g\circ h=f$. Let $i:Z\to Y$ be the scheme-theoretic image of $h$ [def-nagata-scheme-theoretic-image] (the closed subscheme of $Y$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] cut out by $\ker(\mathcal O_Y\to h_*\mathcal O_X)$, through which $h$ factors as $h=i\circ h'$). Then $g\circ i:Z\to S$ is proper and $h':X\to Z$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism]; in particular $h(X)=i(Z)$ is a closed subset of $Y$.

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 0AH6 (lemma-scheme-theoretic-image-is-proper) and its proof (h quasi-compact by Schemes Lemma 03GI lemma-quasi-compact-permanence; h(X) dense in Z by Lemma 01R8 lemma-quasi-compact-scheme-theoretic-image; h(X) closed by Lemma 01W6 lemma-image-proper-scheme-closed; Z proper by Lemma 03GN). Stacks assumes only that $X\to S$ is universally closed; this node states the proper case, which is the one used. The 'in particular' is $h(X)=i(h'(X))=i(Z)$, closed as $i$ is a closed immersion
